draft.title: Life in Sparta
card: Sparta was a Greek city-state that built its society around war. Its citizens were full-time soldiers, so they did not farm or do trade themselves.
Boys
Spartan boys left home at about age seven to join a state training system called the agoge. They learned to fight, to endure hardship and to obey.
Helots
Helots were people held in servitude by the Spartan state. They farmed the land and gave much of the crop to Spartan citizens, which freed the citizens to train for war.
Women
Spartan women had more freedom than Athenian women. They could own and manage property, and they took part in exercise and training.
draft.remember: Sparta was built for war: boys trained from seven, helots farmed, and women had more freedom than in Athens.

a.q: Why could Spartan citizens spend their lives training for war?
opts: Helots farmed the land and supplied their food
Spartan women ran all trade and farming alone
Foreign traders paid Sparta to do its fighting
Boys finished their training by the age of seven
a.why: Helots did the farming and gave much of the crop to citizens, so citizens had time to train. Boys began training at about seven, but that does not explain how adult citizens were freed from farm work.
a.clue: Think about who grew the food.

b.q: A visitor from Athens in the 400s BCE notices that Spartan women own land and exercise in public. What does this show?
opts: Spartan women had more freedom than Athenian women
Spartan women were trained in the agoge as boys were
Spartan women were helots who worked on the farms
Spartan women were treated the same as Athenian women
b.why: Spartan women could own property and take part in exercise, which Athenian women usually could not. The agoge was the training system for boys, so the second option is wrong, even though women did exercise.
b.clue: Compare what Spartan women could do with what the card says about Athens.

a.best: Helots farmed the land and supplied their food

b.best: Spartan women had more freedom than Athenian women

problems.detail: Why (b) refers to 'the second option' as the agoge option, but options are shown in random order (here the agoge option is first). Students may be pointed to the wrong option. Name the option by its content instead.
